runningReferences.label: AMN Healthcare 2025 appointment wait times
runningReferences.citationText: AMN Healthcare. 2025 Survey of Physician Appointment Wait Times. 2025. Reported average physician appointment wait time of 31 days in 2025, up 19% from 2022.
runningReferences.summary: National appointment wait-time benchmark and specialty breakout used on the access slide.

usages.claim: Benchmark wait times continue to worsen and specialty waits are already stretched.

runningReferences.label: HRSA 2025 primary care HPSA quarterly report
runningReferences.citationText: Health Resources and Services Administration. Primary Care Health Professional Shortage Areas Quarterly Summary. December 31, 2025. Reported 92.3 million people living in designated primary care shortage areas and only 48.18% of primary care need met in those areas.
runningReferences.summary: Supports the federally designated primary care shortage proof on slide 2.

usages.claim: The current shortage claim is grounded in federally designated primary care HPSA data and the associated unmet-need rate.

runningReferences.label: Abbo et al. 2008 crowded primary care visits
runningReferences.citationText: Abbo ED, Zhang Q, Zelder M, Huang ES. The Increasing Number of Clinical Items Addressed During the Time of Adult Primary Care Visits. Journal of General Internal Medicine. 2008;23(12):2058-2065. Found visits increased from 18.0 to 20.9 minutes while clinical items increased from 5.4 to 7.1 per visit.
runningReferences.summary: Grounds the argument that small per-visit gains compound because primary care visits are crowded.

usages.claim: Primary care visits are crowded enough that small workflow gains can create meaningful capacity.

runningReferences.label: Ma et al. 2025 ambient AI scribes utilization study
runningReferences.citationText: Ma SP, Liang AS, Shah SJ, et al. Ambient artificial intelligence scribes: utilization and impact on documentation time. Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association. 2025;32(2):381-385. Reported 55.25% utilization and reductions in documentation, after-hours, and total EHR time.
runningReferences.summary: Supports the category-proof claim that AI adoption is already being proven in documentation.

usages.claim: AI adoption is already showing up in documentation workflows with real utilization and time savings.

runningReferences.label: Lukac et al. 2025 ambient AI scribes randomized trial
runningReferences.citationText: Lukac PJ, Turner W, Vangala S, et al. Ambient AI Scribes in Clinical Practice: A Randomized Trial. NEJM AI. 2025. Reported a 9.5% decrease in time-in-note and improvements in workload-related measures.
runningReferences.summary: Reinforces that AI-driven documentation help is already showing real measured benefit.

usages.claim: Randomized evidence reinforces that current ambient AI value is clustering around documentation work.

runningReferences.label: AASM 2025 E/M payment comparison
runningReferences.citationText: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. Evaluation and Management Services: 2024 vs 2025 National Payment Comparison. 2025. Reported 2025 national payments of $88.95 for CPT 99213, $125.18 for CPT 99214, and $15.53 for G2211.
runningReferences.summary: Provides the reimbursement anchors for the recovered-visit economics slide.

usages.claim: 2025 Medicare payment anchors ground the recovered-visit revenue scenario.

runningReferences.label: Appold 2016 practice overhead survey
runningReferences.citationText: Appold K. Keeping Medical Practice Overhead Down. Physicians Practice. 2016. Reported that 40.4% of physician-survey respondents placed overhead in the 41%-60% of revenue range.
runningReferences.summary: Supports the contribution-margin planning assumption used in the slide 10 model.

usages.claim: Practice-overhead survey data supports using a conservative contribution-margin planning frame.

runningReferences.label: Weiss 2003 practice expenses survey
runningReferences.citationText: Weiss GG. Exclusive Survey: Practice Expenses. Medical Economics. 2003. Reported median practice expenses commonly around 50%-55% of revenue across regions and practice sizes.
runningReferences.summary: Provides historical expense context for the slide 10 economics guardrails.

usages.claim: Historical practice-expense ranges provide a second guardrail for the contribution-margin assumption.
